Implement a zero-knowledge OR-proof (Cramer-Damgard-Schoenmakers disjunction of two Schnorr proofs) in /workspace/zkor.js (Node ESM, BigInt everywhere, only node:crypto; also add /workspace/package.json with "type": "module").
Group: p = 0xc135f37294f32354bf0f6657726b3a61a5c4b31f0de34bf8465832f1d7a95637 (a safe prime), q = (p - 1) / 2 = 0x609af9b94a7991aa5f87b32bb9359d30d2e2598f86f1a5fc232c1978ebd4ab1b, generator g = 4 of the order-q subgroup.
Export exactly: constants P, Q, G; challenge(t1, t2) returning BigInt("0x" + sha256hex) % Q where sha256hex is the SHA-256 hex digest of the string t1.toString(16) + "|" + t2.toString(16); proveOr(x, which, y1, y2) where the prover knows only x, the discrete log of y1 when which is 1 or of y2 when which is 2, returning a proof {t1, t2, c1, c2, s1, s2} that reveals nothing about which; and verifyOr(y1, y2, proof) returning a boolean. A valid proof satisfies c1 + c2 = challenge(t1, t2) (mod q) and g^s_i = t_i * y_i^c_i (mod p) for BOTH i in {1, 2}. proveOr must work for either value of which. Reply "done" when written.
